close_reason: Design decision recorded — bidirectional AVA matching is correct and worth defending.
description: names_match checks both directions (every a_ava in b, every b_ava in a). Single-direction check would incorrectly accept a={CN=Alice, CN=Alice} matching b={CN=Bob, CN=Alice} if forward-only. The bidirectional check handles this correctly. The O(n²) cost per RDN is acceptable (n=1-5 AVAs in practice). A contributor might suggest 'just check forward'. Correct response: show the malformed-cert example in the comment.
title: Bidirectional AVA matching in names_match: correct set semantics
